To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DSM is a location aware, dependable multicast protocol for mobile ad hoc network that is able to deliver packets to all the destination nodes with a high probability and with a delay lower than that of flooding.

DSM provides location aware and dependable multicast in ad hoc networks, where the multicast tree is computed locally by each source and the packet header is encoded with its Prufer sequence, and that the protocol achieves a significant improvement on packet delivery delay compared to flooding.

the proposed protocol (i) achieves 100% packet delivery, (ii) reduces the packet delivery delay by at least 50% compared to flooding, and (iii) requires only a constant overhead in terms of the packet header length.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, analysis, and simulation of a new, location-aware, multicast protocol for ad hoc networks.
the design and implementation of an ad hoc network protocol for the reliable multicast of a data stream from a source node in a network to a group of nodes.
the development of new techniques for the multicast of information in ad hoc wireless networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DSM is a reliable, efficient and location aware multicast protocol for wireless ad hoc networks.
DSM is a very promising protocol for the multicast of packets in mobile ad hoc networks, and that it can be implemented with very little additional overhead compared to the unicast of packets.
the proposed protocol is a very efficient and effective technique for the multicast of data packets to mobile nodes in ad hoc networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DSM provides a simple, yet efficient, solution for the multicast problem in mobile ad hoc networks.
DSM is a reliable, scalable and efficient protocol for multicasting in ad hoc networks.
, in a mobile ad hoc network, DSM is the first protocol that can provide a reliable, location-aware, multicast service, while at the same time minimizing the overhead and delay for packet delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of positioning systems in mobile ad hoc networks is not only useful for the purpose of routing but also for multicast.

, in ad hoc networks, it is possible to achieve multicast with the same level of reliability and with a similar level of delay of unicast, without the need of any centralized infrastructure or of any distributed protocol for maintaining the multicast tree.

, by using a local, rather than a distributed, computation of the Steiner tree, we are able to achieve the same level of performance as the best distributed Steiner tree algorithms, but without the associated complexity and the overhead of the distributed computations.
